question: The difference between the ages of Girish and Rohan is 10 years. 15 years ago, Girish was twice as old as Rohan. Find Girish's present age.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant over time. So, 15 years ago, their age difference was also 10 years.

15 years ago, ratio of ages of Girish and Rohan = 2 : 1.

Difference in ratio = 2 − 1 = 1 part.

1 part = 10 years ⇒ Girish's age 15 years ago = 2 parts = 2 × 10 = 20 years.

Girish's present age = 20 + 15 = 35 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference between present ages of Girish and Rohan = 10 years.

15 years ago, Girish was twice as old as Rohan.

**Calculations:**

Let Girish's present age be G and Rohan's present age be R.

⇒ G − R = 10 ⇒ R = G − 10

15 years ago, Girish's age = G − 15 and Rohan's age = R − 15.

According to the question:

⇒ G − 15 = 2 × (R − 15)

Substitute R = G − 10 into the equation:

⇒ G − 15 = 2 × (G − 10 − 15)

⇒ G − 15 = 2 × (G − 25)

⇒ G − 15 = 2G − 50

⇒ 2G − G = 50 − 15

⇒ G = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of any two individuals always remains constant, irrespective of the number of years passed or yet to come.

Ratio Method for Age Problems

When past and future age ratios are given, equate the change in ratio parts to the number of years. Adjust the parts if the difference in ratio terms is not equal.

Linear Equations in Ages

If present age is x, then age n years ago is (x − n) and age after n years is (x + n). This basic logic forms the foundation of establishing correct linear equations.
